title: English for academic purposes
titleCn: 学术英语辅导咨询：语言学习中心设施与论文写作

paragraphs.text: Part three.
You will hear a conversation between a student called Jan and a tutor at the Language Study Centre of his university.
First, you'll have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-six.
Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-six.
Come in. Hello. Are you Jan Tchaikovsky? You've booked an appointment?
That's right.
Well, I'm Vicky McDonald, and I work here in the Language Study Centre.
I wanted to ask you for some advice. I'm a second-year law student.
So you'll have a dissertation next year?
Yes, and I'm really worried about such a long piece of writing.

Well, let me tell you about some of the facilities on offer. First, you can get individual tutorial help. You sign up on the appointment lists outside the English language staff room. Please put your email address so that we can get in touch with you.
Sorry, uh, I don't know where the staff room is.
In the Blackstone Library.
Oh, uh, on the ground floor?
No, it's on the upper level, room three oh one.
And I don't have to pay?
No, it's free to anyone registered with the university. That's excluding anyone paying fees for intensive courses with the language center.
That's a relief.
If you prefer to work on your own, you can always go to the language resources room.
Where's that? I always get lost.
In the Modern Languages building. That's behind Arts C Block by the restaurant.
And is it useful there?
Yes. You'll find a wide range of multimedia resources like CDs and videos with worksheets and learning materials.
Really?
And you'll find advisors there every evening from five till eight thirty if you have any problems.
That's good. So they could look at my dissertation too, could they?
Not really. They're there to guide you around the resources, so you can find the help you need. Do you know that we've also set up a small self-access room in the law department? Have you seen it?
Yes, but I haven't worked there yet.
When you do, we'd be interested in any feedback on how useful you find it. It's a new venture. And you'll find you can access the electronic journals there easily, which will save you a lot of money.
Okay. Well, thanks very much for your help.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions twenty-seven to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-seven to thirty.
Can I just ask you about the classes?
They'll start again in October. Well, there are two courses you might find useful. The first is a class for academic writing.
For all faculties?

Yes. The course concentrates on a number of functions common to academic writing in general. For example, the language you use to describe similarities and differences. And as the course progresses, there will be the opportunity to relate the content to work in your own discipline.
I haven't had too many problems with descriptions, but I've got a problem with writing summaries of cases. Would that be covered too?
Definitely. Let me see. The other functions we concentrate on are cause and effect.
That's always seemed quite straightforward to me, but what I really need is language for making generalizations. Is that on the list?
Yes, it is.
And when I have to discuss things in terms of categories or classes, y-you know, the language for that?
Yes, that's here too. There'll be a lot of opportunity to work on that.
Can I just tell you, I've got quite a few problems in the basic structure of my dissertation. I've no idea how to organize it, what to put at the beginning, for example.

Well, there's a course which lasts a term covering the conventions of academic writing. For example, introductions, as you've just mentioned, and then things like referring to other sources, reporting results, conclusions, and bibliographies.
Good. And could you tell me about the second course you mentioned?
The content is the same, but it takes less time. It's a weekend workshop.
Can I enroll for any of these courses now or when I come back on September the twenty-first?
No, I'm afraid you'll have to wait for the beginning of the academic year. That's anytime in the fortnight from the eighth to the twenty-second of October. Classes begin on the twenty-fifth.
Well, thanks very much for your help. I'm feeling much more positive about my dissertation already.
Good.
That is the end of part three. You now have forty-five seconds to check your answers to Part three.
